title: Visualizing the distribution of black carbon's electron storage capacity using silver
author: Xin, Chiu
materials: Step 2: Silver tagging to locate the ESC

Ag+/Ago has a standard reduction potential (EH0) of +0.80 V vs. standard hydrogen electrode (SHE), which is similar to that of DO at pH 7 (PO2 0.21 atm) and higher than the reported EH0 of quinones at pH 7 [2]. Given the ESC of BC was attributed to quinoic moieties [3,4], it would be thermodynamically favorable for Ag+ to accept one electron from reduced BC to form Ago. Therefore, when Ag+ diffuses into BC and reacts with reduced redox-active moieties such as hydroquinones in the pores, nAg will be formed in situ at or near where the electrons resided. Aqueous Ag+ concentration can be monitored to obtain Ag uptake by BC through reduction as well as adsorption. Since adsorbed Ag+ would not yield Ago nanoparticles, only ESC is tagged by nAg. While various silver salts can be used, precipitation and complexation should be considered. For the same reason, pH should be controlled by either a pH controller or a buffer.

steps.title: Reduce black carbon (fill ESC)
steps.instruction: In an anaerobic glove box using O₂‑free media, prepare a solution of a strongly reducing, negatively charged agent (e.g., Ti(III) citrate or dithionite) at a concentration that provides excess electrons relative to the estimated ESC of the BC sample. Add the BC sample to the solution, using a pre‑determined amount of reducing agent, and incubate until the solution’s electron content no longer decreases (reaction may take hours to days depending on particle size). Then thoroughly rinse the reduced BC with O₂‑free deionized water, vacuum‑dry, and store the dried sample back in the anaerobic glove box. Optional: prior oxidation by prolonged exposure to dissolved O₂ can be performed to drain electrons for ESC quantification, but a fully reduced sample is not required for later tagging.

substeps.instruction: Prepare reducing‑agent solution in DO‑free media inside the glove box.
Add BC sample to the solution with a pre‑determined excess of reducing agent.
Rinse the BC thoroughly with DO‑free deionized water.
Store the dried BC in the anaerobic glove box.

steps.title: Silver‑tag ESC sites
steps.instruction: Still under anaerobic conditions, add an aqueous Ag⁺ solution (any suitable silver salt, taking care to avoid precipitation or complexation) to the reduced BC. Adjust and maintain the pH (≈7) with a buffer or pH controller, because Ag⁺ reduction potential (+0.80 V vs SHE) is similar to DO at pH 7 (PO₂ 0.21 atm) and higher than quinone potentials. Allow Ag⁺ to diffuse into BC; reduced redox‑active moieties (e.g., hydroquinones) will donate electrons to Ag⁺, forming elemental silver nanoparticles (nAg) in situ at the locations of stored electrons. Monitor the aqueous Ag⁺ concentration to quantify uptake that results from reduction (as opposed to mere adsorption).

substeps.instruction: Prepare an Ag⁺ solution in DO‑free media; select a silver salt that minimizes precipitation/complexation.
Adjust the solution pH to ~7 using a buffer or pH controller.
Introduce the Ag⁺ solution to the reduced BC sample in the glove box.
Incubate to allow diffusion and electron transfer, forming nAg at ESC sites.
Measure remaining Ag⁺ concentration to assess reduction‑based uptake.

steps.title: Visualize silver tags by EM
steps.instruction: Prepare the Ag‑tagged BC for electron microscopy. Because silver is much heavier than carbon, nAg can be imaged directly using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), or scanning TEM (STEM). For interior distribution, perform EM tomography or image cross‑sections of BC. Analyze the size, density, and spatial distribution of nAg on the surface and within the interior to infer the spatial distribution of the electron storage capacity.

substeps.instruction: Mount or section the Ag‑tagged BC for EM analysis.
Image the sample using SEM, TEM, and/or STEM.
Conduct EM tomography or cross‑section imaging to access interior sites.
Quantify nAg particle size, density, and distribution to map ESC.
